:::{#def-deviance}
#### Deviance and residual deviance

Let $\llik_{\text{sat}}$ be the maximized log-likelihood
of the saturated model (@def-saturated-model),
and let $\llik(\evb)$ be the maximized log-likelihood of a model $M$
with the same outcome distribution family.
The **deviance** of model $M$,
also called its **residual deviance**, is:

$$
D \eqdef 2\paren{\llik_{\text{sat}} - \llik(\evb)}
$$

When the family has a dispersion parameter
(such as $\sigma^2$ in a Gaussian model),
both log-likelihoods are evaluated at the same value of that dispersion parameter.
:::

::: notes
The likelihood ratio statistics computed with `lrtest()` in this section
estimate $\sigma^2$ separately in each model,
so they are not exactly equal to the deviances in @def-deviance,
which hold $\sigma^2$ at one common value.
:::
